record.title: Croatia restricts non-exempt personal border crossing in March–May 2020
record.scope: Personal crossing prohibition at all border posts; land component retained here
record.crossings: Croatian road and rail frontiers; no claim that every crossing was physically barricaded
record.direction: Both directions under the legal order, with nationality and purpose exceptions
record.movement: Non-exempt personal movement; freight personnel and transit remained permitted
record.exceptions: Croatian return and departure to country of work/residence; EU/Schengen home return; medical, frontier worker, freight, diplomatic, emergency and transit categories. Later business/property exceptions.
record.imposing_authority: Croatian Civil Protection Headquarters; border police
record.enforcement: Original binding order and same-day Hina/HAK report of implementation; no independently observed first traveller at the endpoint.
record.consequences: Ordinary travel restricted; reported delays cannot be attributed solely to Croatian measures.
record.relationship: Separate imposing authority and movement category from neighbouring-country restrictions. Reciprocal policies must not be added as extra border-wide days.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no status inference at 21 October 2026
record.context: Initial 30-day rule was extended and amended. Business/property/urgent travel had already been eased before a nationality-based exemption.
record.uncertainty: 28 May permits citizens of Czechia, Hungary, Austria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Slovenia, Germany and Slovakia. The amendment was published on 29 May but effective on adoption. This is partial legal easing, not all-nationality reopening or a continuous duration.

historical.duration_note: Formal change of permission; operational reopening and continuous effective duration not established. No claim of a continuous nationwide operational closure.
